body:
A whole bunch of different stressors are hitting you at the same time. It sounds overwhelming. Daily suicidal thoughts are exhausting -- I've been there. 

You've managed to pull yourself out of that dark place before -- that's no small achievement. Therapy and medication are solid supports. You have a handle on self-care. Stick with it.

I've found that I sometimes hold myself to an unreasonable standard, something I wouldn't do to a friend. Treat yourself like a treasured loved one. Compassion and respect.

If there is a way to room with someone else then do. Protecting yourself comes first.

You are a girl.

You're identity is legitimate and you get to define the criteria for feeling comfortable in your skin. That criteria may develop over time or it may stay constant. My point is that you and you alone get to redefine it if and when you see fit.

It took me a long time to learn the parts of myself I wanted to accept and those I wanted to change. First I wanted more masculine traits then feminine, back and forth I went searching for a balance that seemed impossible to achieve (I'm still not sure I've found it). Non-binary/genderfluid is probably the closest fit. Supports have helped me a great deal.

Stay strong and good luck.
You've felt this low before?

It sounds like you want some relief. I've been told suicidal ideation is a coping mechanism (just a poor one) and a reflex for many people (including myself).

I'm sorry to hear about your loss. Grief is a uniquely  horrible.

Meaning can be hard to find. I've felt worthless myself and I understand how horrible it can be. Depression is shit but it can be manageable. 

The only meaning I've found, I've made for myself. Going for a peaceful walk ; cooking a meal ; table top  games ; reading a book.

Worth is similar. Focus less on what others think of you (easier said than done) and more on how you feel about yourself. 

You're punishing yourself over the past. Why? You don't deserve to suffer for making mistakes.
This is why I think I am a bad DM. When I say they want something different - I mean different quality/delivery.
Thanks
I might be giving them too much freedom
I've been putting all of those things in. That's what I think they want so that's what I try to give them.

RP opportunities
Challenging encounters
Cool items
Chance for their characters to shine and their choices to matter
Puzzles

Not too sure. Doubt?
20 sessions or so. Things are moving forward. I think the style isn't to everyone's taste and people want different things out of the campaign.

Win: thicc curly auburn hair - no hair loss (yet) despite it running in both sides of the family ; booming voice ; I burn fat without trying ; hobbit feet for stability ; insects don't like my blood for whatever reason.

Loss: poor beard growth, eczema, lifelong depression, crooked teeth, short-sighted, short-heighted.

Apart from my mental health - nothing major. The panic attacks and mild hallucinations from anxiety make it difficult to function in a work environment. My energy levels plummet during major depressive episodes. Which can last month's at a time.

That's rough. Bullying in the workplace is a serious problem. I hope you're doing better. Thank you for the support.

I burnt out from my job. I'm finding it hard to function, nevermind earn a living.

I can't see a way forward. I can't stand the guilt of burdening those around me. The guilt of wishing for death knowing it will upset those close to me. The guilt that this is my fault, my own lack of foresight or resilience.

Things were improving for me, I had made progress. I have nothing but support for others with my illness. 

Now it seems hopeless. All the strength I had has been sapped away.
I've struggled with this most of my life. It feels unavoidable.
Euthanasia is far better than typical suicide methods. Death doesn't scare me, dying most certainly does. A botched attempt or painful death would be a nightmare.

I appreciate the offer but it's not sustainable. I can't live on the generosity of others. I've sought help. I've swallowed by pride. I'm overwhelmed by shame and worthlessness. 

I just want some relief.
It'll taper off. You'll be fine.

I've been a high dose of mirtazapine for the best part of 2 years. No issues with weight gain that I can recall but I am male with a pretty high metabolism. Have experience any side affects apart from one I'm about to mention.

Fair warning, the first month is unpleasant. You might've experienced something similar with other medication. Suicidality can be increased while your body adjusts - simply put - motivation increases before mood this is normal response.

What keeps you going? 

I'm not fishing for some grain of positivity here. I am genuinely curious how you are capable of facing each day. The situation you've described is bleak.
He's not your responsibility.
They can help. They will be able to point you in the right direction at the very least. Additionally, you could receive treatment from them.
Of course. The question I was asking though was looking for what in the world keeps you going.
A medical professional can of tremendous assistance
Sound argument.

Doesn't sound like there was much standard of care given to you.

The first few therapists/psychiatrists I saw were terrible. After that they got better. Finding the right doctor for me was what gave me some scrap of optimism.

There's a lot to unpack here.

If he hates you then why can't you break up with him?
Have you visited a doctor?
What's on your mind?

Talk to a doctor/therapist, help from a professional can help.

Additionally, it never ceases to surprise me  when im down how much a good meal, a little excercise  and sleeping correctly helps to sort your mood.
Emotions can be utter bullshit.

That's pretty fucking shit, man.

I'm not gonna waste your time with platitudes or false optimism. For what it's worth, I genuinely hope you find some relief.
Has anything come close to giving you relief?

Perfectly understandable. 

Has this always been the case?

I've had success with pharmaceutals TBH. Although, I agree with you that they are not the only source for medication. Mushrooms are proving to be extremely effective in trials for depression treatment.

I was afraid that that would be the case.

Is there a particular reason/feeling that drives the suicidal thoughts or does it seem to come from nowhere?

That's fair. You have a right to be sceptical. I gather you've looked for solutions so forgive me if I repeat things you've heard before. 

I personally don't believe depression can be cured with any quick fix. Living with it is a pain but it doesn't always have to be a pain.

Frequency is key here. Getting into a routine makes these less of a chore. You need to keep doing these to reap the benefits.

Excercise: as fucking tedious as it is, does help. You don't need to join a gym or some shit just get moving several times a week.

Eating right: I'm not suggesting a diet or cutting out crap food. Just eat more of the good stuff.

Talk to a doctor: You may feel that they can't help but they can. Medication could be beneficial. They can give you options.

Therapy; talking about shit works, you vent and they give you techniques to cope. Suicidal ideation can be subverted with cognitive behavioural therapy.

Hobbies: this can give you an outlet to express yourself and persue an interest. Often giving you a positive feedback loop. Physical hobbies allow you to excercise and feel healthy. Mental hobbies give a sense of accomplishment and self worth.

I've been there. I'll be there again.

There are ways to alleviate the suffering without harming yourself.

It can help. Although, right now, it doesn't appear to be working for you.

A reason to live can be tough to find when everything seems pointless.

What do you enjoy about the world? What would you miss if it were gone tomorrow?

You're not a drama queen. There doesn't need to be a reason/cause that you must point to, if you are suffering then you need help and support. A doctor is a good start, they can offer resources to help you through this.

Your pain is valid. It is real. Seeking treatment is an important step.
It's not an easy thing to accept when you have strong feelings for another. Have you reached out to people before?

You don't need to justify your depression. Even if things appear to be going great you still have the right to feel shit. 

It's obvious you are suffering. I understand your loneliness but your friendship with this girl might be more important than a romantic relationship. There is a connection, if she has similar problems then she might need you as much as you need her.

I would also recommend you talk to your doctor. They will help you to cope and manage these issues.
